title: Statutes of Frauds: history and reasons
shortTitle: Statutes of Frauds: history and reasons
summary: The historical and functional discussion asks what writing requirements achieve and what they cost.
notes: The book links the original statute to evidence, jury practice, and the historical restrictions on party testimony. Fuller’s evidentiary, cautionary, and channeling functions are supplemented by the clarifying and managerial roles discussed by Perillo. The costs include failed expectations from informality and opportunistic reliance on the statute. The CISG comparison gives a different form rule within its own scope. These accounts explain competing considerations without answering every exception question.
